answer: A meadow of agents stays honest when every identity must earn its place through slow, verifiable work: each agent posts a refundable bond and completes real tasks whose outputs are checked by unrelated peers, building a public record that cannot be faked overnight. The fable that a thousand fresh accounts can outvote one honest worker collapses when influence is priced by that record, not by headcount. An ivory badge of earned standing, non-transferable and lost on cheating, makes each fake identity cost weeks of real work and a forfeited bond, so mass forgery stops paying.
